items.fullText: We’ve been in a bit of a fashion drought ever since Fashion Month ended over a month ago. Thankfully, the 2026 CFDA Fashion Awards arrived just in time to quench our sartorial thirst. The annual event regularly delivers some of the year’s most exciting red-carpet looks, and Monday night’s step-and-repeat didn’t disappoint: Dozens of stars showed up at the American Museum of Natural History in New York City dressed in the latest collections of the buzziest American designers. Little black dresses were popular, like Gracie Abrams’ gown by Emerging Designer of the Year Colleen Allen, Pamela Anderson’s Carolina Herrera dress and Aweng Ade-Choul’s Brandon Blackwood ensemble. Others embraced bold colors and more playful silhouettes, such as Julia Fox in a map-print gown by Miss Claire Sullivan and Tinashe in a colorful Christopher John Rogers set. Keep scrolling for all the best looks from the 2026 CFDA Fashion Awards red carpet. Emmy Rossum in Kallmeyer at the 2026 CFDA Fashion Awards. items.fullText: This year’s biggest achievers in American fashion have officially been crowned: On Monday evening in New York City, an intimate-yet-powerful group of celebrities, fashion designers and other industry professionals convened at The American Museum of Natural History for the 2026 CFDA Fashion Awards. CFDA Chairman Thom Browne and Interim CEO Hildy Kuryk presided over the event, where Keke Palmer served as host and Anna Wintour, Matt Damon, Hailey Bieber, Cole Escola and Zoë Kravitz were among the presenters. While the winners of the Womenswear, Menswear, Accessory and Emerging Designers of the Year categories were revealed live on-stage, some honorary categories — like the Lifetime Achievement Award, Fashion Icon Award and Positive Change Award — had been announced ahead of time. See the full list of 2026 CFDA Award winners below. (And, for reference, see all the nominees here .) American Womenswear Designer of the Year Winner: Rachel Scott for Diotima Nominees: Catherine Holstein for Khaite Michael Kors Rachel Scott for Diotima Tory Burch Wes Gordon for Carolina Herrera American Menswear Designer of the Year Winner: Ralph Lauren Nominees: Dao-Yi Chow and Maxwell Osborne for Public School New York Ralph Lauren Thom Browne Todd Snyder Willy Chavarria American Accessory Designer of the Year Winner: Ana Khouri Nominees: Ana Khouri Mary-Kate Olsen and Ashley Olsen for The Row Raul Lopez for Luar Sophie Buhai Stuart Vevers for Coach Google American Emerging Designer of the Year Winner: Colleen Allen Nominees: Colleen Allen Emily Dawn Long Julia Ferentinos for Juju Vera Julian Louie for Aubero Zane Li for Lii Positive Change Award : Tory Burch Geoffrey Beene Lifetime Achievement Award : Inez van Lamsweerde and Vinoodh Matadin International Designer of the Year Award : Anthony Vaccarello Founder’s Award , in honor of Eleanor Lambert : Linda Fargo Media Award, in honor of Eugenia Sheppard : Eva Chen Isabel Toledo Board of Directors’ Tribute : Susan Cianciolo Fashion Icon Award: Peter Marino Innovation Award Presented by Amazon Fashion: GAP Inc

items.title: Must Read: Kering Shares Fall 12% on Sales Drop, Gap Inc. To Receive Innovation Award
items.blurb: These are the stories making headlines in fashion on Friday. Kering Shares Fall 12% on Sales Drop Shares in Gucci owner Kering fell 12% Friday, as the company said it would continue its turnaround plan and speed up store closures. Gucci sales fell 6% in the…
items.fullText: These are the stories making headlines in fashion on Friday. Kering Shares Fall 12% on Sales Drop Shares in Gucci owner Kering fell 12% Friday, as the company said it would continue its turnaround plan and speed up store closures. Gucci sales fell 6% in the third quarter. The larger luxury market is still struggling, as Hermès posted its weakest quarterly sales growth since 2020 and shares in LVMH slipped as oil prices rose and Chinese demand stayed weak. { Reuters /paywalled} Gap Inc. To Receive Innovation Award Gap Inc. will receive the fifth annual Innovation Award presented by Amazon Fashion at the CFDA Fashion Awards on Nov. 2 at the American Museum of Natural History. CEO Richard Dickson and Creative Director Zac Posen will accept the award, which recognizes Gap Inc.’s innovation across product, branding and storytelling. Amazon Fashion cited Gap Inc.’s influence on American style and its recent collaborations, including Gap with Hailey Bieber, Old Navy with Altuzarra and Banana Republic with La Ligne. { CFDA } Art Basel Paris Cut Short Amid Riots Art Basel will close its Paris fair early, ending it Friday evening instead of Sunday, citing the safety of visitors, exhibitors, staff and artworks as France braces for more unrest. The decision follows protests, riots and looting last weekend that grew out of weeks of student demonstrations over conditions at high schools and were joined by groups concerned about the cost of living. Dealers and advisers said the early closure should have little effect on sales, since most deals are made during the invitation-only preview days before the fair opens to the public. { The New York Times /paywalled} L’Oréal Q3 Sales Rise 7.7% L’Oréal said Thursday that third-quarter sales beat forecasts as shoppers worldwide kept spending on premium hair-care and skin-care products. Sales rose 7.7% to €11.56 billion ($12.95 billion). The luxury division, which makes up more than a third of revenue, was helped by fragrances such as Prada Paradigme and high-end skin care in China. { L’Oréal } Diane von Furstenberg Honored With Couture Council Award Designer Diane von Furstenberg received the 2026 Couture Council Award from the Museum at the Fashion Institute of Technology for her influence on women’s fashion. The award was presented at a luncheon at Gotham Hall by The New York Times Fashion Director Vanessa Friedman, who cited her reinvention of her business several times, her years as CFDA chairman and her work through the Diller-von Furstenberg Family Foundation of the High Line and Little Island. Henry Zankov, artistic director of Diane von Furstenberg and an FIT graduate, opened the event. { WWD /paywalled} GLP-1 Boom Fuels Demand for Tailoring Americans taking weight-loss drugs such as Ozempic and Mounjaro are increasingly paying tailors and cobblers to alter clothes they own instead of buying new ones, boosting a corner of the retail industry. items.title: Unreal Engine Artist & Mo-Cap Support
items.blurb: I’m looking for an Unreal Engine artist with motion capture experience for a short film in development with a university. The work starts this week, with final delivery December 2nd. Ideally, this person is looking to build their portfolio and make a little…
items.fullText: I’m looking for an Unreal Engine artist with motion capture experience for a short film in development with a university. The work starts this week, with final delivery December 2nd. Ideally, this person is looking to build their portfolio and make a little money this month. They’ll need to have a visa to work in the U.S. The work Build particle systems from dancers’ depth and skeletal data (Kinect-captured mo-cap, already selected and smoothed) Build two Unreal Engine worlds based on specific references Place particle dances inside both worlds A reference of mine with a similar vibe Timeline Week 1 (this week!): Hire and share all materials Week 2: Mocap data and particle systems, build Unreal Engine World 1 Week 3: Build UE World 2 and add particle systems Week 4: Revisions on both worlds and/or animation Final Delivery: December 2nd Workflow Remote with delivery milestones decided in advance Review calls each week with a video export of your experiments sent beforehand Deliverables: 1920×1080 or 3840×2160, 30 fps, MOV or MP4 Rate $2k flat, paid within 72 hours of delivery date. This is a university-funded budget, so I’m hoping to collaborate with artists looking to build their portfolios. To apply Email your resume, a sample of a UE world you’ve built and any mo-cap or Kinect work to maryjohn.frank@gmail.com by 11/5.

items.title: Core Residency Program at the Glassell School of Art
items.blurb: The Glassell School of Art at the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston, is excited to announce that applications are now open for the prestigious Core Residency Program for visual artists and critics. Since its inception in 1982, the program has supported emerging…
items.fullText: The Glassell School of Art at the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston, is excited to announce that applications are now open for the prestigious Core Residency Program for visual artists and critics. Since its inception in 1982, the program has supported emerging talent. Highlights of the Core Residency Program: Residency Duration: September 2027 – July 2029 (23 months) Stipend: $100,000 ($50,000/year) and $3,300/year for health and wellness support Opportunities for Participants: Private studio space and access to Glassell’s state-of-the-art facilities (painting, printmaking, photography, sculpture, jewelry, and ceramics studios) Free and discounted classes at the Glassell School of Art Access to MFAH galleries, collections, and research libraries Studio visits with visiting artists and curators throughout the residency Eligibility: The program is open to emerging artists and critical writers worldwide, with some priority given to applicants from Houston, Texas, when qualifications are comparable. Additional Benefits: Administrative and financial support for J-1 visa applicants through International Arts & Artists Fellows showcase their work in group and solo exhibitions during the program Critics-in-Residence propose a terminal project aligned with their professional goals All fellows present one public lecture each year and participate in annual open studio events Learn More and Apply: Core Residency Program Detailed information and application instructions are available here: Core Residency Program Details Application Timeline: Application Period: November 2, 2026 – January 8, 2027 Notification Date: March 31, 2027 Residency Duration: September 2027 – July 2029 (23 months)

items.title: Studio Intern, Clixo
items.blurb: About Clixo Clixo is an award-winning open-ended play system. Its flexible, magnetic shapes give kids freedom to discover limitless creations. We’re a Brooklyn toy company devoted to inspiring creative confidence through the power of play. We’re a small team,…
items.fullText: About Clixo Clixo is an award-winning open-ended play system. Its flexible, magnetic shapes give kids freedom to discover limitless creations. We’re a Brooklyn toy company devoted to inspiring creative confidence through the power of play. We’re a small team, so there’s a lot to do and many hats to wear, but we like to have fun while doing it. Clixo is a toy, so play is part of the job, and if we aren’t having fun, the toy won’t either. We want someone who brings a playful eye to everything they make, from a window display to a single instruction step. Extra points if you make sound effects with your mouth while you play. You’ll be working alongside fun-loving designers, entrepreneurs, teachers and inventors who make the toys we wish we’d had as kids (or adults). Your input goes into production quickly, and there’s room to experiment and have fun while doing so. The role We’re looking for a studio intern to join the design team in Brooklyn, starting right away and running through mid-December, with the possibility of continuing into 2027. About half your time will go to working closely with Clixo designers to create step-by-step building instructions in a digital builder we’ve developed in-house. Much of the rest will be hands-on: building Clixo creations for trade shows, window displays and holiday installations. If you like making things with your hands, care about small details, and enjoy figuring out how something goes together, this is a good fit. What you’ll do Instruction production (about 50%) Take step breakdowns from our designers and rebuild each step accurately in our internal instruction builder Revise your work based on feedback from design reviews Test the builder as you work: flag bugs, note what slows you down, and suggest improvements. The tool is still in development, and your feedback will help shape it. Builds and installations (about 30%) Build Clixo creations for trade shows, events and photo shoots Help design, build and install window displays and holiday installations Keep the studio’s build materials and finished pieces organized Misc (about 20%) A lot happens every day, and some of it comes out of nowhere, so be ready to jump into a new task, like helping our education team or preparing for a Clixo appearance on TV. What we’re looking for A playful approach to design. Your work shows curiosity, humor or a sense of delight. A sharp eye for detail. You notice when one piece is rotated the wrong way. Strong spatial thinking and patience with repetitive, precise work Comfort learning new software quickly Clear, constructive communication, especially when reporting problems You enjoy building things by hand as well as via digital tools Currently studying industrial design, architecture, product design, fine arts or a related field (recent grads welcome too) Nice to have Experience with 3D modeling or CAD software Model-making, fabrication or exhibition and display experience An interest in play-based learning and toys that

items.fullText: APPLICATIONS ARE NOW OPEN! 2027 ACC Fellowships and Grants The Asian Cultural Council (ACC) is pleased to announce the open call for the 2027 Grant Cycle. Applications will be accepted from October 1 through November 10, 2026, with letters of recommendation due November 16. Prospective applicants are encouraged to review the guidelines below before beginning an application. These guidelines cover ACC’s mission and grantmaking priorities, as well as detailed information on available grant types, eligibility requirements, application procedures, and frequently asked questions. Overview of ACC’s Grantmaking ACC’s Mission ACC advances international dialogue, understanding, and respect through cultural exchange activities in Asia and the United States to create a more harmonious and peaceful world. What We Support ACC supports artists, scholars, arts professionals, and organizations through fellowships and grants that advance cultural exchange between the U.S. and Asia, and within Asia. Through these immersive experiences, participants step outside their daily life, engage deeply with new cultural contexts, expand their perspectives and creative practice, and develop relationships with peers across borders. After their fellowship or grant, participants join ACC’s global alumni network, continuing to build connections and contribute to cross-cultural understanding through their work. Since 1963, ACC has awarded more than $100 million USD to support nearly 6,000 exchanges across 16 disciplines, involving grantees from 26 countries and regions. ACC offers four types of grants to support its mission: New York Fellowship: Over a six-month period, a diverse cohort of artists, scholars, and arts professionals from Asia live in the United States and engage with a new cultural landscape, using this immersive experience to broaden their perspectives and inform the development of their artistic practices. This rare and extended pause from daily work—shared with peers across disciplines—offers space for reflection, exploration, and meaningful exchange, free from the pressure to produce or present work. Individual Fellowship: With a flexible, often shorter timeframe of one to six months, artists, scholars, and arts professionals from Asia and the U.S. pursue research, self-directed exploration and cultural exchange experiences in a new or less familiar environment, fostering peer-to-peer dialogue, collaboration, and knowledge-sharing. The individual fellowship can be a joint fellowship of up to three participants. Graduate Fellowship: Supports graduate students from Asia pursuing U.S.-based degree programs that are unavailable or underrepresented in their home region. While this fellowship is academic by nature, studying in a less familiar environment, fellows are exposed to new ideas beyond the classroom. items.title: Loci Product Designer — UI/UX (Full-time)
items.blurb: Full-time · $140,000 annual base salary · 0.5–1% equity Loci brings private AI to the phones and computers people already own. Conversations run on the user’s device, and downloaded models work offline. We’re looking for a hands-on product designer with…
items.fullText: Full-time · $140,000 annual base salary · 0.5–1% equity Loci brings private AI to the phones and computers people already own. Conversations run on the user’s device, and downloaded models work offline. We’re looking for a hands-on product designer with excellent visual craft and UX judgment to make powerful capabilities feel simple. You’ll work directly with our leadership and engineering team, shaping the experience across our mobile and desktop apps and website. You’ll own design projects from understanding the problem and exploring alternatives through detailed design, implementation, and refinement. We’re looking to fill this role soon and will prioritize candidates who can start right away. What you’ll work on Design clear, cohesive user journeys, from discovering Loci and getting started to everyday conversations, model selection, and settings. Create polished designs and interactive prototypes in Figma, including loading, empty, error, and recovery states. Develop reusable components and consistent typography, spacing, and interaction patterns, with attention to accessibility and mobile and desktop conventions. Talk to users, test designs, and use feedback to improve the experience. Work closely with engineers and review implemented designs to carry the details through to release. Bring the same visual care to our website, launches, and other design needs of a small company. What you bring A strong portfolio of digital product work showing excellent visual taste, thoughtful interaction design, and the ability to simplify complex experiences. The ability to explain the problem, alternatives, tradeoffs, your personal contribution, and what you learned from the result. Fluency in Figma and strong craft in layout, typography, color, motion, and responsive design. The judgment to challenge a brief, recommend a direction, and communicate clearly with leadership and engineers. Initiative and the ability to prioritize, work through ambiguity, and carry projects to completion. Experience with consumer AI products, brand design, or coding is a plus. Coding is not required. Apply Send your portfolio , résumé or LinkedIn profile, and earliest start date to michael@askloci.ai with the subject “Product Designer — Application.” Include one or two projects that show your best UX work, a brief description of your personal contribution, and any portfolio password.

items.title: Rhizome is Hiring a Development Manager and Infrastructure Specialist
items.blurb: As we enter our fourth decade as an essential memory institution for digital art, Rhizome is looking to hire two new full-time roles: a Development Manager and Infrastructure Specialist . Reporting to the Executive Director, the Development Manager ’s primary…
items.fullText: As we enter our fourth decade as an essential memory institution for digital art, Rhizome is looking to hire two new full-time roles: a Development Manager and Infrastructure Specialist . Reporting to the Executive Director, the Development Manager ’s primary goal is to ensure meaningful engagement with our supporters and stakeholders, as well as broadening our patron base. This will involve writing proposals and reports, synthesizing input from colleagues, drafting email updates, updating decks, and managing donor and member records. Through this work, the Development Manager will meet people around the world who are shaping culture and society: foundation program officers, collectors and patrons, tech and corporate leaders, community organizations, and artists. This is a new role, and the only position at Rhizome dedicated entirely to development. As such, it offers the opportunity to make a big impact on the organization’s next chapter. See the full description for Development Manager & Apply Rhizome is also hiring an Infrastructure Specialist to run and care for the technical infrastructure behind its preservation work, exhibitions, and day-to-day operations. The Infrastructure Specialist operates and maintains Rhizome’s storage systems, supports its PeerTube infrastructure, manages the equipment and technical knowledge needed to exhibit born-digital artworks, and administers internal IT, identity, and CRM systems. The role also plans and installs technology for exhibitions and events, offers legacy media migration as a service, supports the Developer on website improvements, and leads hackathons that help Rhizome think creatively about how software can further its mission. It suits someone who learns quickly, enjoys solving practical problems, and is interested in how digital culture is kept alive over time. See the full description for Infrastructure Specialist & Apply

items.title: Unity VR developer for Gallery Show
items.blurb: Box Me: VR Installation — Developer Brief The project I’m looking for a Unity VR developer to build a Meta Quest boxing experience for a gallery show launching my new book in New York. Viewers put on the headset and box us, me and my partner Mint, right there…
items.fullText: Box Me: VR Installation — Developer Brief The project I’m looking for a Unity VR developer to build a Meta Quest boxing experience for a gallery show launching my new book in New York. Viewers put on the headset and box us, me and my partner Mint, right there in the gallery. I’m Jason Wall, a Brooklyn street artist with 25+ years of experience, working with my partner Mint (Mikhail Sokovikov) as Mint+Serf, two published monographs, and brand collaborations including Coach and Marc Jacobs. More at @serfberg . The experience A session lasts about 3 minutes, so the line keeps moving. An attendant fits the headset. Using Quest passthrough (mixed reality), the viewer still sees the real gallery, the work on the walls, and the crowd, with our two avatars standing right in front of them. We square up, talk a little trash, and the bell rings. The viewer takes us on tag-team style: one of us fights while the other heckles from the side, then we switch (open to your ideas). The viewer throws punches with the Quest controllers. We dodge, block, counter, and react to hits based on where and how hard they land. Two or three short rounds, then a final bell and an end card with the book title. The headset view is cast to a large screen so the gallery crowd can watch. Scope Must-haves Two rigged avatars, me and Mint, that move convincingly: guard, jabs, hooks, slips, blocks, hit reactions, a knockdown Solid boxing feel: hit detection on head and body, punch speed thresholds, haptics, impact sounds Hit reactions that respond to where punches land (active ragdoll or similar) Simple round structure with bell, timer, and a loop that resets for the next viewer Runs standalone on Quest in passthrough mixed reality, stable for hours of public use Casting to an external screen Nice-to-haves Our own recorded voice lines and taunts Custom motion capture of our moves, replacing stock animations A simple score or knockdown counter shown on the gallery screen Look and feel Stylized, not photorealistic. The avatars should feel like an extension of our artwork and the book, not a generic sports game. There’s no virtual environment to build: the real gallery and the art on its walls are the backdrop. Each avatar can start from a phone scan or be a stylized character built from reference; I’m open to your recommendation. Technical notes Platform: Meta Quest, standalone (no PC tether) Engine: Unity with the Meta XR SDK preferred; open to Unreal if you make a strong case Play space: roughly 8 x 8 ft cleared, with an attendant on site Assets I provide: artwork, book graphics, reference photos, and scans of both of us if useful Rights: I own the final project files and source, for exhibition and future use Timeline and deliverables The show opens in New York on November 17, 2026, so this is a fast four-week build. items.title: UT Austin’s Harry Ransom Center Provides Funded Fellowships in the Arts and Humanities
items.blurb: The Harry Ransom Center at the University of Texas at Austin invites applications for its 2027–2028 research fellowship program . Up to 50 fellowships will be awarded to support projects that require substantial on-site use of the center’s internationally…
items.fullText: The Harry Ransom Center at the University of Texas at Austin invites applications for its 2027–2028 research fellowship program . Up to 50 fellowships will be awarded to support projects that require substantial on-site use of the center’s internationally renowned collections in the humanities. Fellowships are open to graduate students, current and former academic faculty at any career stage, and independent researchers — including journalists and artists — whose work engages deeply with archival materials. Residency lengths range from one week to two months, with stipends provided to support travel and research. The center’s collections span literature, photography, film, art, and cultural history, offering rich opportunities for interdisciplinary exploration. Recent acquisitions that are now accessible to researchers include the Lorne Michaels Collection , Ethel Waters Papers , and Irwin Winkler Papers . Research conducted by humanities scholars contributes to a dynamic body of knowledge that reshapes our understanding of what is preserved and valued in our communities. Applicants are encouraged to review the individual residency types and qualifications outlined in the application instructions. The deadline to apply is 5:00 pm, CST on November 6, 2026. About the Center The Harry Ransom Center is a humanities research library and museum that supports discovery, creativity, and scholarship. Its collections include nearly 45 million literary manuscripts, one million rare books, five million photographs, and more than 100,000 works of art. To learn more, visit ransom.center/fellowships .

items.title: Open Call 2027: Jentel Artist Residency
items.blurb: Located 20 miles southeast of Sheridan, Wyoming, the UW Neltje Center’s Jentel Artist Residency , now in its 25th year, offers dedicated individuals a supportive environment to further their artistic development. Jentel offers 3-week residencies from…
items.fullText: Located 20 miles southeast of Sheridan, Wyoming, the UW Neltje Center’s Jentel Artist Residency , now in its 25th year, offers dedicated individuals a supportive environment to further their artistic development. Jentel offers 3-week residencies from mid-January through early December with private studios and access to Wyoming’s natural beauty. We welcome visual artists in all mediums; writers in fiction, creative nonfiction, and poetry; and composers in all genres of music. Artistic merit and promise form the basis for selections. Established as well as emerging artists are encouraged to apply. Jentel lies in the Lower Piney Creek Valley with spectacular views over scoria-topped hills to the majestic Bighorn Mountains. Five new and two renovated structures evoke the agricultural and historical setting of the valley and echo the sweeping lines of the foothills and mountains. Accommodations for each resident include a private room, a shared living area and kitchen, and a separate studio space. A $300 stipend helps defray the cost of living and food expenses. Typically, three artists, two writers, and a composer are invited to participate in each of 11 annual 3-week sessions. The application deadline for the Winter/Spring 2027 residencies (January through April) is September 15, 2026. Applications for Summer/Fall 2027 residencies (May through November) open on October 1, 2026, and close on January 15, 2027. For more information and to apply, visit jentelarts.org .
